speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what support is available to SMEs; and (b) what are the options available to affected businesses, when their utilities costs have increased by large factors due to the insolvency of their previous utilities retailers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The price of LNG, or spot Liquefied Natural Gas, rose significantly and remains elevated at more than three times the levels as at the start of 2021.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: While our piped natural gas (PNG) supply typically helps to moderate the impact from higher LNG prices, there was a series of disruptions and planned depletions to our PNG supply since the second half of 2021.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This confluence of factors has resulted and caused increased volatility in wholesale electricity prices.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Since October 2021, EMA, or the Energy Market Authority, has implemented a set of measures to enhance Singapore's energy security and stabilise SWEM, or Singapore Wholesale Electricity Market, prices.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Nevertheless, some market participants were adversely affected by the volatility.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: All affected households and businesses with an average monthly consumption of less than four megawatt hour (MWh) can switch to Singapore Power's regulated tariff at any time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Some businesses consuming four MWh or more managed to secure plans with other retailers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There remains about 11,000 business consumer accounts – accounting for about 1% of consumers – which have to buy electricity directly from the Singapore Wholesale Electricity Market, or SWEM, and are thus exposed to more volatile electricity prices.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To help these businesses, EMA worked with the generating companies, or gencos, to offer monthly fixed price plans under the Temporary Electricity Contracting Support Scheme, or TRECS for short, in January this year – that is, last month.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The TRECS plans were fully subscribed for January.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For the month of February, the initial offering of TRECS was also fully subscribed.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We encourage all consumers without a retail plan to consider taking up these contracts for greater certainty.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Singapore imports all of our energy and cannot be fully insulated from developments in the global energy market.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Well, let me make a correction – Singapore imports a vast majority of our energy, not all of our energy.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The higher fuel prices feed into our electricity bills to reflect the higher costs of electricity production.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I had mentioned during the Committee of Supply debates last year, we had been enjoying artificially low electricity prices for several years due to an over-investment in capacity and fuel by the gencos.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I have also alluded to the fact that that was also below the cost of generating electricity; and thus, it was not sustainable.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In fact, if Members of the House remember, I also put up a chart that clearly demarcated and showed that the cost of generation was higher than the cost of the electricity tariffs at that time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: An electricity price correction was, therefore, unavoidable and the current global energy crunch has precipitated and exacerbated this correction.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Again, Members of this House would have asked what help is, therefore, available for the affected businesses.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Household and small consumers which need help with their electricity bills can apply to SP Services for instalment payment plans.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Businesses which need financing support can also make use of ESG's programmes, such as the Temporary Bridging Loan and Enterprise Financing Scheme SME Working Capital Loan.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The 11,000 or so business accounts without a long-term retail contract bear the brunt of the electricity crunch.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To help them weather the storm, EMA has worked with gencos and electricity retailers to reduce the volatility and lower the cost of buying electricity through TRECS, additional monthly contracts offered by gencos, and on the wholesale market for businesses, as I had mentioned earlier.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For example, Sembcorp Power Pte Ltd is offering one-month fixed price plans at preferred rates to consumers with average monthly consumption of between four and eight MWh.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: EMA will also continue to monitor closely market developments, including heightened geopolitical tensions and their potential impact on global energy prices, and put in place the necessary measures to secure our energy supply, enhance stability and ensure the orderly functioning of the market.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Over the last 20 years, our energy market has served us well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our electricity supply is one of the most reliable and price-competitive amongst major developed cities.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our energy market is now being tested by unprecedented shocks and volatility in the global energy markets.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Nevertheless, we are committed to ensuring that Singapore's power supply remains secure and reliable, and to supporting our vulnerable customers during this period.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: My only exhortation and urging is for all consumers to use energy prudently and to adopt energy conservation as a way of life.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will also learn from this episode to see how we can strengthen and fortify our energy reliance, resilience and our electricity market.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And I am confident that, together, we will emerge from this stronger.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I am very heartened to hear from the Minister that TRECS will be extended and also that there are more fixed monthly plans available to the SMEs; the shocks have been quite real for our SMEs because some were hit about three times.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While we all understand that, we are takers of energy prices.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, on Minister's last plea, can I ask this question of MTI: what measures are in place to support our companies and, especially our SMEs, in terms of moving to more sustainable practices as well as better energy consumption practices?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: The reason I ask this is because in resource-scarce Singapore, where we are moving more to automation and digitalisation, our companies are actually relying more on energy.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: So, it is good that we are focusing on reliance, resilience of our infrastructure – and we must – but we need to also help our companies pivot and move to being more energy-efficient as well.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: I hope the Minister can share with us what measures will be in place to support them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There are quite a number of initiatives that we have moved on to.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have encouraged many businesses to consider using energy-efficient power systems, including energy-efficient light bulbs and even air conditioning.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have worked very closely with MSE where we would encourage companies to use devices or appliances with the triple-tick marks to improve energy efficiency and conserve energy.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have also started giving grants to help companies to pivot into using more solar photo-voltaic panels.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On top of that, over at EMA, given the fact that we do not have a very constant and consistent supply of solar energy, we are also, in parallel, developing a series of energy storage systems in the form of ESS, so that, during the time when there is peak solar power, we can store up that energy to allow it for use later on.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On top of that, in terms of the building of efficiency, we have encouraged industries to go green, where they can use natural ventilation, to even working with design consultancy firms in the entire built environment to see how we can actually reduce the need for lowering the temperature in terms of using the air conditioning.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There are multiple initiatives and they are probably too numerous for me to go through at length.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These are just some very clear examples of what we have started to work with the industry on.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Several businesses in my constituency have shared with me they are shocked at seeing their electricity bills jump threefold or more despite their efforts to reduce electricity usage.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Businesses with consumption of more than four MWh but less than 20 MWh, which include many neighbourhood kopitiams, have to buy electricity from SP Group at the wholesale electricity price, which is very elevated and volatile now.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: They are also facing difficulty buying electricity from retailers because many retailers are not offering contracts until later in the year or even next year.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If this is not possible, can EMA allow these SMEs to buy at the regulated tariff instead, so that their operational costs do not skyrocket?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: How many businesses have applied for, during these two months under TRECS, but were not able to obtain contracts?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Are there plans to expand the number of slots in TRECS available for those who need it?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Can I answer the second question, and then I will go back to the first one?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have shared earlier on in my main reply to a Parliamentary Question, for February, there still remains about 200 megawatts, and I was encouraging many of these SMEs to consider going into this particular retail plan.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our estimates also tie in, generally, with the consultants, and these are global market consultants, who look at the trend of energy prices.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Of course, we hope that the situation in Eastern Europe, namely, between Russia and Ukraine, does not get worse.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But once winter is over, we are cautiously optimistic that natural gas prices will ease somewhat.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we may not need to extend TRECS beyond six months.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At this particular point in time, we are monitoring the situation very, very closely.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In fact, we do not monitor on a month-to-month basis, but we monitor it on a weekly basis, and, sometimes, even on a daily basis.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I do not have the data for how many businesses have not been able to subscribe to TRECS in January but, as a follow-up, what I can do is to try and get the statistics and then answer that either in another Parliamentary Question that the Member can file later, or I will see how to get that answer across.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are also contemporaneously working with gencos to see if they can offer additional temporary discounts at their end.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These offsets will not be able to help account for the price increase completely.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because, as I have said before in the past, this has gone up by threefold since the start of 2021.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But, certainly, it will go some way to help companies to adapt to the sudden surge in prices.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: There is one question which I think was not answered, which is, is it possible for EMA to allow SMEs to buy – I am talking about SMEs which use between four MWh and 20 MWh of electricity a month – at the regulated tariff, instead of at the wholesale electricity price?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The reason why we created TRECS was because we took into consideration the fact that, to expect Singapore Power, or SP, to suddenly open it up to everyone for them to buy, I think SP may have difficulty in supplying all that incremental needs in the short run.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we need to also understand how the market works.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: SP has contracted a limited quantity of such long-term electricity contracts and we have to reserve them for households, for small business consumers, who, traditionally, do not have the bargaining power to negotiate for better retail prices.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This will then cause the regulated tariffs to rise.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, all households and small consumers, who are, today, on the regulated tariff would then have to bear the costs of price stability for the large consumers.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: It seems that we have an idea of how many businesses are affected by the exit of all these gencos.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: But this increased business cost adds to the cost pressures on goods and services in general and this, ultimately, goes down to consumers and individuals or residents in the end.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, I would like to know, does the Ministry or the Government track or study the impact that this episode has actually had on the cost of living for individuals?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And what are the findings of any such study?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I do not have the answer at this particular point in time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I understand the concerns that the Member has.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If I may humbly request that she file a Parliamentary Question.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We, certainly, will look into it and, probably, give her a more robust and detailed answer.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, can I ask the Minister, is that the constraint why we cannot expand this TRECS scheme further to even larger consumers?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The first point in terms of the S-LNG, the emergency supply, the stock pile, whether it has become a constraint, the answer is no.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have shared many times, for natural gas, we are sufficiently provided for and we will ensure that we continue to monitor very closely and, if necessary, invest in infrastructure to continue to make sure that our energy resilience and our sufficiency in terms of supplies will not be compromised.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To the Member's question why larger companies cannot enter into longer-term contracts rather than on a month-to-month basis, it is, I think, because of the volatility in terms of the prices as well as the uncertainty that is evolving today, large companies which want to enter into contracts are now entering into contracts at new, very high-priced levels.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If they were to lock in long-term contracts of a year or two years today, and if the stability comes back to some level of normality, they may find that they are at a disadvantage.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Then, would they want to unwind the contract that they had gotten themselves into?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Likewise, from the gencos' perspective, they are also not sure whether they can continue to buy or procure gas at current spot prices.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In the event that they procure and they sign up, and the spot prices go up even further, they would take a bigger loss and a bigger impact.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, it is that kind of bottlenecks that we have today.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And so, that is why EMA has stepped in to see how we can manage for the current volatility, on a short-term basis, by offering these one-month temporary retail electricity contracts.
